frameworks.name: VORP Core

install_commands.import_sql: Import vorp_core.sql + oxmysql schema into MySQL/MariaDB server
install_commands.npm_build_if_applicable: cd resources/[vorp]/vorp_character/ui && npm i && npm run build

sql_major_tables: vorp_characters (characterId, identifier, job, jobgrade, money, gold)
client_exports_common: vorp_core:Notify(title, msg, type, durationMs) -- Toast notification
server_exports_common: vorp_core.AddUser(source) -- Insert new player row on first join
frameworks.character_creation_model: vorp_character provides native-dressed character creator UI with sliders; wardrobe persists to vorp_clothing
frameworks.inventory_type: vorp_inventory: slot-based UI with metadata JSONB support; item images in html/img
notes: Open source RedM framework with largest shared module ecosystem
Has a modular lib API + prompt/blip/notification wrappers
Supports framework-specific and shared helpers
Primary DB: MySQL/MariaDB via oxmysql (ghmattimysql legacy also works)
Discord: https://discord.gg/vorp

frameworks.name: RSG Core

install_commands.import_sql: Import rsg.sql from repo root into oxmysql DB
install_commands.copy_cfg_example: Copy rsg-core/config.lua.example to config.lua; fill framework defaults

sql_major_tables: rsg_players (citizenid, license, money, job, gang, metadata)
frameworks.character_creation_model: rsg-core ships with qb-clothing inspired creator; skin stored in metadata JSON column
frameworks.inventory_type: rsg-inventory: weight (not slot) system with ox_lib inspired UI; item images in web/build folder
notes: Modern RSG variant of popular FiveM-style QBCore patterns ported to RDR3/RedM
GitHub org has many related repositories: shops, jobs, gangs, housing, craft
Useful for cross-framework abstraction docs
Written mostly in Lua with React UIs for major menus
Discord: https://discord.gg/rsg

frameworks.name: RedEM:RP

install_commands.import_sql: Import .sql files from each /SQL subfolder in install order (base, identity, inventory)
install_commands.copy_configs: Copy each config.example.lua to config.lua per module

sql_major_tables: redemrp_characters (char_id, identifier, firstname, lastname, job, jobgrade, money)
client_exports_common: redemrp_menu_base.CreateMenu({...}) -- Scaleform prompt menus w/ auto-prompts
frameworks.character_creation_model: redemrp_identity walks user through name/age selection; then character creator screen
frameworks.inventory_type: redemrp_inventory: simple list UI with counts; metadata support added in v2.2+
notes: Rebooted 2023 ecosystem; original was RedEM (2019) -> today is RedEM:RP
Public framework org and related modules
Important for compatibility docs if supporting legacy RedEM servers
DB adapter: mysql-async (oxmysql compatible wrapper exists)

frameworks.name: Native Scripts ns-lib
ensure_order_server_cfg: ensure ns-lib -- must be FIRST before ns_* or custom framework modules
frameworks.sql_database_prefix: ns_ (optional; most modules share tables with active fw)
client_exports_common: RegisterPrompt(slug, {text, key, hold, enabled, visible, group}, entityOrCoords, onCompleteCb, onTick)
NSBlip:Create({sprite, colour, label, coords, scale, shortRange})
server_exports_common: NSFramework.Bridge() -> auto-detects vorp|rsg|redem and returns shim object
frameworks.character_creation_model: Delegates to whatever underlay framework is running (VORP/RSG/RedEM). Ships char creator in full NS suite.
frameworks.inventory_type: Can provide its own inventory or wrap VORP/RSG/RedEM inventories via same public interface
frameworks.bridge_mode_note: The ns-lib:Bridge() shim normalizes 90% of framework surface (jobs, items, money) so scripts can be cross-framework with zero changes.
notes: Cross-framework abstraction layer; goal: write once runs on VORP + RSG + RedEM + standalone
Supports multiple inventories and SQL adapters
Useful as a compatibility baseline when authoring AI-created resources
RegisterPrompt is the #1 used helper in ns-lib

frameworks.name: Standalone / Raw Natives (no framework)
ensure_order_server_cfg: (no order requirements; standalone resources depend on nothing except game)

install_commands.template: Create fxmanifest.lua with: client_scripts, shared_scripts, server_scripts; ensure <name>

client_exports_common: You provide your own via exports() in fxmanifest.lua
server_exports_common: You provide your own via exports() in fxmanifest.lua
common_events: Cfx base: onResourceStart / onResourceStop / playerConnecting / playerDropped / playerJoining
frameworks.character_creation_model: None; you must build char select from PED natives + menu NUI
frameworks.inventory_type: None; build from scratch using ITEMSETS natives + NUI
notes: Useful for tiny utility resources: dev tools, blip replacers, weather/time controller
All 4 framework entries above ultimately call the same 7,600 RDR3 natives documented in hashes.json > native_namespaces

detecting_framework_at_runtime: if GetResourceState('ns-lib') == 'started' then USE ns-lib.Bridge() for cross-fw shim
interop_notes.fxmanifest_dependency_declaration: dependencies { 'vorp_core' }  -- forces load order; swap for rsg-core/redem_roleplay/ns-lib
interop_notes.money_units: All four frameworks standardize on: money = USD cash 1899, gold = gold dust/coins (1 gold ~20 USD circa 1899)
